title: What is known about 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE---: it halts (Lean).
intro: This six-state machine is on the bbchallenge list of holdouts. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on. The headline: it halts from blank tape, proved in Lean.
verdict: It halts, proved in Lean (theorem halts_from_blank). The machine is a small rewriting system on the right half of its tape (the visit law, kernel-checked): blocks 000/100 are binary digits, blocks 1010 double the visits passing through, and a visit that meets 1011 halts. A checker for this system, proved correct in the kernel, finds that rounds 1 to 161,210 only rewrite and that round 161,211 meets 1011; that evaluation is by native_decide (compiled code), in ten segments.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweeps of the run
claims.text: The shift rules the machine uses in its run (every sweep met when the symbolic simulator runs from many configurations of the run), each for every number of copies.

claims.title: Both counters' increments, for all sizes
claims.text: At an event (A on cell 3; left of it the block 011001 and the left counter in digits 0110 = 0 / 0111 = 1; right of it the phase cell, the block 001010000 and the right counter, digits three cells apart): the left increment with a carry over n ones (22n+34 steps), the right increment on a lowest 0 (42) and over k+1 ones (6k+48), carries across one junk unit 1010000 (84, 90) and across j units then k+1 ones (36j+6k+54). 6 theorems.

claims.title: The visit law, in two forms
claims.text: A visit (the head on a 0 with a 0 on its left and a stream s on its right, in state C or F; it returns in state A two cells further left) rewrites the stream by 0 s → 1 s, 100 s → 000 v(s), 110 s → 000 v(s), 1010 s → 1010 v(v(s)), and halts the machine on 1011 s; for every stream and every left tape. Form W obeys the rules for 0, 100, 1010, 1011; it has no such rule for 110 (W_1100: 1100 s → 1010 v(s)). The run is a sequence of rounds 0^inf A> 1 0 0 S → 0^inf A> 1 0 0 v(1 0 S), starting after 6 steps with S = 1 0^inf.

claims.title: The abstract visit law and its count laws
claims.text: The four rules and the halting pattern as inductive relations on streams, with no machine in them; the 1010 rule is guarded (the stream behind must not start with 11), and after two visits a stream never starts with 11. Under n visits, 000 r and 100 r are binary digits that pass every second visit on, and 1010 r passes 2n visits on; likewise for "one of the first n visits halts".

claims.title: A checker for the visit law, proved correct
claims.text: scan carries a count of visits, kept as the pair e, c for 2e − c, through a finite word in one pass; hscan looks for a halting visit. Both are proved against the abstract system.

claims.title: If the checker accepts, the machine halts
claims.text: This machine satisfies the law, so for every k: if the checker runs k rounds from the word 1 and then finds a halting visit in the next round, the machine halts from blank tape. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

claims.title: The machine halts from blank tape
claims.text: check 161210 [true] = true: rounds 1 to 161,210 use the four rewriting rules only, round 161,211 meets 1011. Evaluated with the checker compiled to native code, in ten segments chained by a kernel-checked lemma (about 3 hours of computing in all; the word grows to 1,001,253 cells). With the claim above: the machine halts. Besides the three standard axioms the theorem depends on eleven native_decide axioms, one per evaluation (trust in the Lean compiler). The number of steps is not computed. Each segment was checked on 13 and 14 November 2026, and the whole check was run again from start to end on 14 November 2026 (HALT CHECKED). The repository's automatic checks cover the kernel-only part, not this evaluation.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 248 cells have been visited and 98 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct run of 1011 steps (longrun.c, the simulator of tools/c/tm.h) without a halt.

claims.title: The left side is clockwork
claims.text: Between consecutive left-end extensions the busiest cell turns 3·2<sup>k</sup> times, each count twice (48, 96, 96, ..., 3·2<sup>22</sup>), in the first 1.5·10<sup>9</sup> steps.

claims.title: How much of the run the increments cover
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps (879,588 events) 95.5% of the events are instances of these theorems (left 439,766; right0 219,887; right1 92,325; junk_10 57,511; junk_110 28,751; junk_jk 1,733); the other 39,615 are carries over other junk layouts and the moments around the ends.

claims.title: The same round as the PR59 machines
claims.text: The three machines of busycoq PR59 (1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- and two relatives) obey the same law with one form of visit, and PR59 proves in Rocq that they halt in round 161,211. The proof here does not use PR59; our C simulator of the law (vis.c) also halts in that round on the PR59 machine. The twin 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE--- has its own theorem: machines with related tables are not claimed to halt together.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.075). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).

claims.title: Two counters of the same events
claims.text: Read off the run: the counters on the two sides of the engine both go up by 1 at every visit of the head to the engine, one of them with fixed junk stretches between some digits; the junk is written when a carry reaches the end of the tape.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Yes, it halts, and Lean has checked the proof. Behind two counters ticking together this machine is a small rewriting system: blocks 000/100 that act as binary digits, blocks 1010 that double the visits passing through, and a block 1011 that stops the machine. For 161,210 rounds the trap never forms; in round 161,211 it does. Nobody could watch that happen: the number of steps is far beyond any direct simulation.

facts.text: halts_from_blank, proved in Lean (kernel + native_decide for the checker run).
The machine as a rewriting system on streams; the checker and its correctness proof.
The first round in which a visit meets 1011.

sections.eyebrow: The whole machine in a few rules
sections.heading: The visit law
html: Forget the states for a moment. Call everything from some cell to the right a stream. Whenever the head stands on a 0 with another 0 behind it and a stream in front, in state C or F, it comes back out in state A two cells further left, and the only thing that has changed is the stream. That excursion is a visit, and what it does depends only on how the stream begins:

the stream beginsafter the visitLean
0 s1 sV_0
100 s000 then one visit to sV_100
110 s000 then one visit to sV_110
1010 s1010 then two visits to sV_1010
1011 sthe machine haltsV_1011_halts

So a block 000/100 is a binary digit: it passes every second visit on. A block 1010 is a doubler: it passes every visit on twice. A block 1011 is a trap. In this machine form W obeys the rules for 0, 100, 1010 and 1011 but not the one for 110, so the 1010 rule is only used when the stream behind the block does not start with 11. Lean proves that this can only matter in the first two visits to a stream, and the checker tests it every time.

The run from blank tape is a sequence of rounds: the tape is 0∞ A> 1 0 0 S, and one round puts 1 0 in front of S and makes one visit. After k rounds S begins with about k/2 doublers, so about 2k/2 visits reach the word behind them, where the digits count them down again. Nothing in the first 161,210 rounds ever produces 1011.

sections.heading: A checker that Lean has proved correct
html: Round 161,211 cannot be watched step by step: a single round near the end makes astronomically many visits (more than 21000). But a count of visits can be carried through the word in one pass. Through a doubler the count doubles; through a digit it halves, and the digit ends up as the count's parity. Keeping the count as a pair e, c that stands for 2e − c makes every such step a few small-number operations.

That pass is a 20-line program, scan. Lean's kernel checks a proof that whatever scan returns is what the rewriting rules give, and that the rewriting rules are what the machine does. What is left is to run the program for 161,210 rounds and see it report a visit to 1011 in the next one. That run is about 1011 list operations, too many for the kernel, so Lean compiles the program and trusts the result of the evaluation (native_decide). It is done in ten segments, so that each can be checked on its own.

The same round as three sister machines. The machines that busycoq PR59 proves to halt (in Rocq) obey the same law and halt in the same round, 161,211. The proof here is independent of PR59, which makes the agreement a useful cross-check. The twin machine 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE--- has its own Lean theorem.

sections.heading: Two counters and an engine
html:
Most of the time the tape is L · engine · R. Each visit of the head to the engine is an event, and every event adds 1 to both counters. In the reference machine of the family (1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC---), L is written in blocks of four cells, 0101 for a 1 and 0001 for a 0, lowest digit next to the engine, and R keeps one cell per digit, three cells apart (the cells 9, 12, 15, … right of the head), lowest digit nearest the engine. Nine consecutive events of the reference machine right after its left-end visit at step 1,571,372 (the head in state A on the bold cell):

This machine is a relative in different clothes: its left counter has 4-cell digits x011, its left-end extensions come after exactly 3·2k turns of the busiest cell, each count twice, and at its left-end visits the tape is that of the reference family: at step 14,008,454 its 183-cell tape agrees with that of 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA--- at step 9,617,068 in all cells but the first two.

sections.heading: The left side is clockwork
html:
When L overflows, the carry runs to the left end of the tape, the tape grows by two cells there, and L starts again. The lowest digit of L is the cell where the head turns most often, and the number of its turns between two consecutive left-end extensions follows a strict pattern, without a single exception in the first 1.5·109 steps (ymax.c):

48 96 96 192 192 384 384 … 3·221 3·221 3·222

So the periods of the left side are powers of two in events, each length twice (the counter gains one digit every two periods). The time per event is not constant, because a carry on the right costs more when it crosses junk, so the steps between left-end extensions grow by factors between about 1.35 and 2.05 instead of exactly 2.

sections.heading: A counter with junk between its digits
html: The cells that change between events are the digits of the counters: each digit changes about half as often as the one before (chg.c counts, over a whole period, how often each cell changes from one event to the next). On the right, between some digits of R, there are stretches of fixed cells (0101010101 00 1 00 1 00 1 and the like) that the carries cross without changing. They are written when a carry runs into the end of the tape, at irregular event counts, and their layout is what makes the run irregular. How they are produced is not decoded yet.

sections.heading: The dangerous moments
html: The machine halts only in state F reading a 1, and F is entered from C1 (0RF) only. After C1, used about 2.9·107 times in 109 steps, the head has read a 0 every time (F0 is used exactly as often). Unlike the other members this machine has no rare transition: every transition is used more than 107 times in 109 steps. Halting would need that ordinary step to find a 1. In every run short enough to simulate directly this has not happened. The proof above shows that it does happen, in round 161,211.

sections.heading: Eight machines, one mechanism
html: The family (G11-Y): 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RF_0RC--- (the reference), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD1RB_0RC--- (the same run), 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_0RD0LC_0RC---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RF_1RB0RD_0RB---, 1RB0LB_0RC0LF_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD0RF_0LA--- (all with left-end extensions after 2k events, each twice, to within a few hundred steps of each other); 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA0RE_1RE--- and 1RB0LB_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB1RB_0LA1RB_1RE--- (the same right part, a differently written left counter); and the mirror case 1RB0LB_0RC0LD_1LD1RE_0LA0RB_0RD1RF_1LA---, with the junk on the left.

sections.heading: The increments, proved for every size
html: This machine runs the reference's two counters with other words: the left digits are 0110 (0) and 0111 (1), the engine blocks are 011001 and 001010000, and the right counter with its junk units is the reference's. lean/Events.lean proves each kind of visit to the engine for every size. In the first 108 steps 95.5% of the 879,588 visits are instances of these theorems.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.075). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.067).
After 109 steps the tape spans 248 cells (86 left of the start, 149 right), with a density of 1s of 0.395.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

summary: Halts (Lean, with native_decide for the evaluation of a verified checker): a rewriting system on streams (visit law, kernel-checked) whose round 161,211 meets the halting block 1011; the same law and round as the busycoq PR59 machines, proved here independently.
